# `tfctl harness exec`

The `tfctl harness exec` command runs a child command such as a coding agent with session-scoped delete permissions.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl harness exec --allow-delete=RESOURCE_TYPES -- COMMAND [ARGS...]
```

## Description

The `tfctl harness exec` command runs a child command with a short-lived, session-scoped permission that lets nested tfctl invocations perform non-interactive deletes.

This is a deliberate, per-session opt-in by a human. The permission is tied to the lifetime of this process and auto-reverts to the safe default (deletes require an interactive confirmation) as soon as the child exits.

This is a safety rail, not a security boundary: the child runs as the same OS user, so a true guarantee that an agent cannot delete must come from the API token permissions set by the server.

## Arguments

- `COMMAND` - (Required) The command to run, specified after a `--` separator
- `[ARGS...]` - (Optional) Arguments to pass to the command

## Available options

The `tfctl harness exec` command supports the following options.

| Option | Description | Default | Required |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `--allow-delete=TYPES` | Specify resource types that nested processes may delete noninteractively. Only resource types that are explicitly named may be deleted noninteractively. Can be repeated or accept a comma-separated list. See supported resource types below. | None | Yes |

### Supported resource types

The `--allow-delete` flag accepts the following resource types:
- `agent-pools`, `agents`, `authentication-tokens`, `cidr-range-lists`
- `explorer-saved-queries`, `gpg-keys`, `hyok-configurations`
- `notification-configurations`, `oauth-clients`, `oauth-tokens`
- `organization-memberships`, `organizations`, `plan-exports`
- `policies`, `policy-sets`, `projects`, `provider-sets`
- `registry-modules`, `registry-provider-version-platforms`
- `registry-provider-versions`, `registry-providers`
- `reserved-tag-keys`, `run-tasks`, `run-triggers`
- `ssh-keys`, `stacks`, `team-projects`, `team-workspaces`
- `teams`, `vars`, `varsets`, `workspaces`

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Examples

### Allow an agent to delete workspaces and variables

The following command allows a coding agent to delete workspaces and variables for one session:

```shell-session
$ tfctl harness exec --allow-delete=workspaces,vars -- opencode
```

### Multiple resource types with repeated flags

The following command allows deleting multiple resource types using repeated flags:

```shell-session
$ tfctl harness exec --allow-delete=workspaces --allow-delete=vars --allow-delete=run-tasks -- bob
```
